- [2023/05/30] Route Handlers are used to create custom request handlers for specific routes using Web Request and Response APIs.
- [2023/05/30] Route Handlers are only available inside the app directory and should not be used together with API Routes.
- [2023/05/30] Supported HTTP methods for Route Handlers include GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS.
- [2023/05/30] Static Route Handlers are evaluated by default with the GET method and can be used for generating custom handlers for files like robots.txt, rss.xml, and sitemap.xml.
- [2023/05/30] Dynamic Route Handlers are evaluated when using the Request object with GET, any other HTTP methods, or Dynamic Functions like cookies and headers.
- [2023/05/30] Route Handlers can use Dynamic Segments for request handlers from dynamic data, but generateStaticParams() is not supported.
- [2023/05/30] Route Handlers support both Edge and Node.js runtimes with an isomorphic Web API.
- [2023/05/30] Route Handlers can be used for revalidating static data, reading cookies and headers, handling redirects, streaming responses, and returning non-UI content.
- [2023/05/30] Route Handlers use the same route segment configuration as pages and layouts, with options like dynamic, dynamicParams, revalidate, fetchCache, runtime, and preferredRegion.
